segments.text: You found an outlier.
segments.caption: You found an outlier.

segments.text: Just delete it, right?
segments.caption: Just delete it, right?

segments.text: Not so fast!
segments.caption: Not so fast!

segments.text: Delete the wrong one, and you lose the most important point in your data.
segments.caption: Delete the wrong one, and you lose the most important point in your data.

segments.text: Here are seven ways to treat outliers.
segments.caption: Here are seven ways to treat outliers.

segments.text: Step zero: ask why it's there.
segments.caption: Step zero: ask why it's there.

segments.text: Is it a mistake, or real but rare?
segments.caption: Is it a mistake, or real but rare?

segments.text: The answer picks the treatment.
segments.caption: The answer picks the treatment.

segments.text: If it's a mistake, fix it.
segments.caption: If it's a mistake, fix it.

segments.text: An age of two hundred and fifty? The form says twenty-five. Correct it!
segments.caption: An age of 250? The form says 25. Correct it!

segments.text: Can't recover the real value? Fill it in, usually with the median, so you keep the rest of the row.
segments.caption: Can't recover the real value? Fill it in, usually with the median, so you keep the rest of the row.

segments.text: If a row doesn't belong, like a test account, remove it, and note why.
segments.caption: If a row doesn't belong, like a test account, remove it, and note why.

segments.text: If it's real, you have four options.
segments.caption: If it's real, you have four options.

segments.text: First, cap it. Anything past the fence gets pulled back to the fence.
segments.caption: First, cap it. Anything past the fence gets pulled back to the fence.

segments.text: The sixty-minute jam becomes forty-two.
segments.caption: The 60-minute jam becomes 42.

segments.text: It still counts, but it can't dominate. This is called winsorizing.
segments.caption: It still counts, but it can't dominate. This is called winsorizing.

segments.text: Next, transform it, usually with a log.
segments.caption: Next, transform it, usually with a log.

segments.text: On a log scale, each step is ten times bigger. That squeezes a long tail in.
segments.caption: On a log scale, each step is ten times bigger. That squeezes a long tail in.

segments.text: Skewed salaries become balanced, and the mean works again.
segments.caption: Skewed salaries become balanced, and the mean works again.

segments.text: Or leave the data alone, and use robust tools: ones that barely react to extreme values.
segments.caption: Or leave the data alone, and use robust tools: ones that barely react to extreme values.

segments.text: Use the median and IQR instead of the mean and standard deviation.
segments.caption: Use the median and IQR instead of the mean and standard deviation.

segments.text: The outlier stays. It just can't drag your results.
segments.caption: The outlier stays. It just can't drag your results.

segments.text: Or keep it and study it.
segments.caption: Or keep it and study it.

segments.text: A two lakh payment at three AM could be fraud.
segments.caption: A 2 lakh payment at 3 AM could be fraud.

segments.text: Here, the outlier is the whole story! Flag it, dig in, and report it separately.
segments.caption: Here, the outlier is the whole story! Flag it, dig in, and report it separately.

segments.text: Here's the complete picture.
segments.caption: Here's the complete picture.

segments.text: Mistakes: fix, fill, or remove.
segments.caption: Mistakes: fix, fill, or remove.

segments.text: Real values: cap, transform, go robust, or keep and study.
segments.caption: Real values: cap, transform, go robust, or keep and study.

segments.text: And the golden rule: if you're unsure, run it with and without the outlier, and report both.
segments.caption: And the golden rule: if you're unsure, run it with and without the outlier, and report both.
